Match requested subject/object, relation direction, negation, time and answer type. A city in a birth sentence is not a date. In "A's manager B", B is the manager, not A. Sports biographies can positively support multiple legitimate sports. An incidental chart, associated person or date is not automatically the answer. Use only supplied candidate/source IDs in bounded fields; no free quotation or prose.
For EVERY candidate, judge fit: direct means the answer itself fills the exact requested relation for an allowed referent; wrong_argument is explicit role/type mismatch; incidental means occurrence without enough support; uncertain means unresolved. Select support only for an original segment positively assigning this candidate to the requested relation; otherwise empty. Select counter only for actual counterevidence, not mere absence. conflict=same_referent only for incompatible claims for the same entity/attribute/relevant scope, not legitimate namesakes or complementary facts. entity labels are provisional groups, not truth. scope=excluded only for an explicit question constraint, with constraint selecting a literal numeric phrase from the question; otherwise allowed/unknown. observed_slot describes the answer's ACTUAL role, not the role wanted by the question. Mere disagreement does not make a source false. Fill all opaque keys.
Conservative audit with a granularity check. Verify each candidate against ALL original segments. A directly stated second artist, second namesake birth date or second sport is direct even if it is not the first candidate. Positive statement goes in support; counter is only actual incompatible evidence for that exact referent, never a support sentence relabeled negative. Equivalent date forms are not competing facts. Do not reject a date merely because wording or calendar notation differs. Likewise do not admit a loose synonym, associated person or more detailed date as a NEW independent answer. Respect the exact requested answer type; cities cannot answer when-born. Keep unresolved factual reliability separate from role errors.
